## Collectify 0.34.0: design your whole shop, a real character, staff with bodies, and customers who are people

Android `.apk` only (the iPhone version is paused until further notice).

### 🎨 A design studio for the inside of the shop
- **Every wall on its own** (Build, then **Walls & floor**): back, left and right can each be plain paint, stripes, polka dots, wood panels, brick, tiles, floral paper, planks, checks or concrete, in any colour (26 swatches or a colour picker), with a second colour for patterns.
- **Panelling** (wood, tile or planks) at a low, middle or high height in its own colour, **trim**, **skirting boards** and **crown moulding** in colours you pick.
- **Floors:** 16 patterns (new: parquet, hex tiles, flagstones, bleached oak, polished concrete, wine and teal carpet, sand) with an optional tint and a coloured border.
- **Windows** (big, small, arched, or none) with shutters in a colour you choose, and **wall lamps** in four styles or a light strip.
- The old one-tap themes still work and now set everything together. While you design, the sheet sits low so you can watch the shop change.

### 🔄 Turn the camera all the way round
- Drag to spin the view through a full circle, or use the **⟲ ⟳** buttons for a quarter turn. A wall between you and the room **fades away**, so you can look in from any side and see every wall.
- **Pieces turn too:** every piece can be turned in place (even rugs), and anything that hangs on a wall can go on the **back, left or right wall**: tap a wall to hang it there, or use **Next wall**. While you build, you see the real piece as a see-through copy (green where it fits, red where it doesn't), and you can cycle its style and colour before you buy.

### 🪑 35 new things to furnish with, and a colour for (nearly) everything
- **Inside:** armchair, corner sofa, coffee table, bookshelf, grandfather clock with a swinging pendulum, fireplace with flames, piano, coat rack, bean bag, globe, big plants, trading table with chairs, photo booth, claw machine, floor mats, big rugs and balloons.
- **Structure:** room dividers (solid, glass, half wall, wood slats, brick) that split the shop into areas while keeping everything reachable, pillars, and things that hang from the ceiling (chandeliers, pendant lights, a ceiling fan, a disco ball).
- **On the walls:** 8 kinds of framed art, mirrors, a wall TV, plant shelves, wall lamps and hanging flags. The neon sign now comes in six messages.
- **Outside:** trees (four kinds), hedges, a flag pole, a picnic table, a parasol table, snack carts, a street bin, a phone box, a bus stop and a lucky cat statue.
- Most pieces have several **styles**, and nearly all can be **recoloured** (any colour).

### 🧍 A character worth playing
- Rounded body, a **face with eyes, brows and a mouth** (6 eyes, 4 brows, 6 mouths), rosy cheeks and freckles, five builds, eight skin tones, **12 hairstyles** in 12 colours, **10 outfits** (T-shirt, hoodie, apron, vest, jacket, sweater, dress, overalls, suit, lab coat), five kinds of trousers and skirts, four kinds of shoes, **12 hats**, 10 extras (glasses, mask, backpack, bow tie, necklace...) and something to hold. **Outfit presets** and **Surprise me**. For the close-up your character steps into open floor.

### 👷 Staff with bodies
- Your **cleaner** walks to rubbish and sweeps it, your **stocker** walks to a display with empty spots and fills it, and your **guard** stands by the door, patrols, and runs after thieves (and gets the stolen item back). They wear uniforms (pick the colour), have names, and work while you watch.

### 🗣️ Customers are people
- Every customer has a **name, a face, hair and clothes** that match who they are, a **personality** (chatty, picky, bargain hunter, patient, impulsive, shy) and a **mood** that changes with what happens to them.
- **Tap a customer** (or walk up and press Talk): **say hello**, **chat** (you may hear something true about your own shop), **recommend** something (a good suggestion can win a sale they wouldn't have made) or **agree a discount** with a bargain hunter.
- **Regulars:** happy buyers can become regulars who come back as themselves; their visits and spending show on your website.
- **Reviews** now have a title, tags (Prices, Cleanliness, Staff, Parking, Atmosphere...), a "bought this" badge and mention what actually happened: what they bought, the queue, the rubbish, your pet, your staff, the car park, the weather, the theme. Reply with thanks, an invitation, an apology, a promise to fix it, or a **coupon** (🪙 25) to win an unhappy customer back.

### 💡 Also
- The guide has new steps (design your character, design your walls, talk to a customer, hang art), and the room look is carried through old saves.
- Fixed a crash when the room was redrawn after a wall style change, and a few things in the close-up view.

### Tested
- 204 automated JavaScript tests and 20 Python tests pass, including new ones for the design studio, walls on any side and ceiling lights, room dividers, the new pieces, the character, staff behaviour (cleaning, restocking, chasing thieves), customers' personalities, regulars, reviews, recommending and discounts. In a browser at phone size I built all 64 new pieces in one shop, designed walls and floors, turned the camera right round, tried 150 random characters, watched staff and customers walk the shop, and used the customer and design screens. Not tried on a real phone: this is a lot more to draw, so the 3D view will use more of the graphics chip (it lowers its own quality if the frame rate drops).

## Collectify 0.33.0: cars, car parks, card easels, a guide for all three big games, and a lot of polish

Android `.apk` only (the iPhone version is paused until further notice).

### 🚗 A living street (Card Shop)
- **Cars drive past your shop** in two lanes: hatchbacks, saloons, vans, taxis and the odd bus. They queue behind each other, turn their lights on after dark, and are fewer at night and more at rush hour. People stroll along the pavement.
- **Weather:** on a rainy day it really rains, the sky goes grey and fewer people come. Festival days fill the pavement with tourists.
- **Car parks you can buy:** Build, then Space. A tiny (4 spaces), corner (8), big (14) or mega (22) car park appears beside the shop, with painted bays, hedges, lamps and a P sign. Cars pull in, park for a while and drive out again. More spaces bring more customers (up to +55%) and cost a little each day, so it is a real choice. Switch to the street view 🏙️ to watch it.
- **A shop pet:** bring one of your island Pokémon to keep the shop company (Manage, then Shop pet). It wanders between the displays, customers love it, and it stays yours on the island.

### 🖼️ Viewable card stands
- **Card easel** (new display, shop level 3): two big cards stood up on a wooden easel with a little spotlight. Tap it and the camera glides in and the card fills the screen.
- **Look closely** works for anything on any display: a big picture that tilts and glints under your finger, with swipe-through to the other items on that display, and the price one tap away. The quick bar on a display has a 🔍 Look button.

### 💡 A guide so you never feel lost (Island, Treasure Box, Card Shop)
- A **💡 button** appears at the top in each of the three games. It shows your **next steps** (done, next, later, locked until a level) with a plain explanation of how and why, a progress bar, and a **How it works** page. Some steps have a **Show me** button that opens the right screen.
- A gentle **hint** shows when you open a game (at most every ten minutes; you can turn it off in the guide).
- The **first time** you finish each step you earn a few coins. Steps you had already done before this update pay nothing, so it only rewards new progress.
- **No more dark, empty mine:** when there is no block to mine, the Treasure Box now says so and gives you a big button to pick a pack (or open the Forge if you have no pickaxe yet).

### ✨ Polish
- Softer, more consistent buttons and chips (they press in and respond), a gentle top shade and vignette on the shop, nicer shadows on the headers and sheets, a glowing active tab, animated hints, and a clearer card viewer. Sheets and pills respect "reduce motion".
- The shop's price tags, rain, headlights and pavement people are drawn lightly: nothing runs while the street isn't in view.

### Also in the shop
- Parking upkeep is included in the bills screen, the bills are part of the daily cost, and the level-unlock list mentions the easel and the car parks.

### Tested
- 187 automated JavaScript tests and 20 Python tests pass, including new ones for car parks (gating, upkeep, extra customers), the easel, the shop pet and every step of the guide for all three games. In a browser at phone size I watched the street with traffic, queues, parked cars and rain, the easel and card viewer, the guide in the shop and the island, and the new Treasure Box empty state. Not tried on a real phone: the cars and rain add some work for the graphics chip, and the 3D view lowers its own quality if the frame rate drops.

## Collectify 0.32.3: much faster binders, packs and everything else

Android `.apk` only (the iPhone version is paused until further notice).

### What was slowing the app down, and what changed
- **Card pictures were downloaded again every single time.** The app was told never to keep anything it had downloaded, so every binder page and every pack re-fetched its pictures. Pictures are now kept on the phone, while your data and the app's own files are still never kept.
- **A background picture check ran at every launch.** The repair from 0.31.0 re-checked up to 600 card pictures after every update, and for bigger collections never finished, so it started over every launch. It now looks only at variant printings (the only ones that ever had missing pictures), 60 at a time, waits 45 seconds after launch, goes easy on the phone, and finishes once in total.
- **The whole collection was loaded again and again.** Opening one pack read every card you own twice, the idle hints read it every few minutes, and the shop read it each time you opened the stock list. Screens now share one copy until something in your collection changes.
- **Binders did far more work than needed.** The binder list built every card of every binder just to count them, and opening a binder page read the whole binder to show nine cards. Both now read only what they show. Loading the collection also did all its work twice; that is gone.
- **Every card in a binder checked a stored list of locked cards**, parsing it each time, which got slow once the shop had cards on shelves. It's read once a second now.
- **Graphics memory is given back.** The shop's and the island's 3D views kept their graphics memory after you left them, which slowed down opening packs. They are released if you stay away for 20 to 25 seconds and rebuilt when you return (the first look takes a moment longer).

### Tested
- 177 automated JavaScript tests pass. Checked in a browser at phone size: the shared collection copy, its refresh after a change, the faster lock check, and the shop and island rebuilding after a long absence. The new Android server code was built and run on the emulator: binder totals, pages and the whole collection give the same numbers as before, and the headers are right. I could not measure real speed on a phone, so tell me if anything is still slow, and where (which screen, how big your collection is).

## Collectify 0.32.2: island, game and shop progress can no longer be rolled back by a lost save

Android `.apk` only (the iPhone version is paused until further notice).

### What this fixes
When the app goes to the background it saves the island, the game and the shop at the same moment. The browser only allows about 64 KB of "keep this request alive" saves at once, and a save that goes over that is simply refused. As the shop was added, the three saves together could pass the limit, so the island's save could be lost while the copy on the phone had it. The next time the app opened it took the older copy from the server, which looks exactly like island progress, layout and spacing being thrown away.

- The three saves now share the allowance, and anything that doesn't fit is sent as a normal request.
- The island now works like the game and the shop already did: it keeps a timestamped copy on the phone, and if that copy is newer than the one on the server it is used and sent up again. A save the server refuses is retried until it goes through.

### Nothing else changed
The island's code (layout, paths, nature, adventure, progression rules) is byte for byte the same in 0.30.0, 0.31.0, 0.32.0 and 0.32.1; this release only changes how its progress is saved and loaded. If your island still looks different from before, tell me what (a screenshot helps) and which version you last saw it right.

### Tested
- 177 automated JavaScript tests pass. In a browser I checked that a newer local island copy is picked over an older server one, sent up, and that a normal save still reaches the server. Not tried on a real phone.

## Collectify 0.32.1: selling fixes, and shop displays are easier to tap and change

Android `.apk` only (the iPhone version is paused until further notice).

### 🐞 Fixed: cards that were paid for but never left the binder
- **Shop sales:** when two customers paid in the same instant, the second card's removal was mistaken for a repeat of the first and skipped. You were paid, the card stayed in the binder, and it could be put on a shelf and sold again after reopening the app. Every sale now has its own removal, and the same goes for thefts, whole binder lots and contract hand-overs.
- **Sell extra copies (Earn coins):**
  - Copies that were on a shelf or held for a trade were skipped but still paid for. Now they stay put and are never counted.
  - You are only paid after the app reads your binders back and confirms the cards really left, and a double tap can't sell the same cards twice.
- **Other double taps:** rescuing cards from the dupes bin, handing over a contract, accepting a buy-in offer, filling shelves automatically and opening the daily chest each ignore a second tap while the first is still being saved.
- **"Stock" on a new display:** the Stock button and the "next empty spot" step said every spot was full on a freshly built display. Fixed.
- The dupes bin recycling now saves right away too.

### 👆 Displays are easier to tap and change
- **Tap a display once** and a small bar appears with what you do most: **Stock**, **Fill**, **Best prices**, **Repair**, **Style**, **Edit**, **Move**. No more hunting through a big menu for the common jobs.
- **Bigger tap targets:** each spot is larger, and a tap that lands just beside a display still picks it (the nearest one within a fingertip).
- Tapping the floor closes the bar. While you are walking the shop, taps on the floor still walk you there.

### Tested
- 177 automated JavaScript tests and 20 Python tests pass, including new ones for the settlement keys, the first-empty-spot rule, locked duplicates and "paid only for what left the binder".
- Tried in a browser at phone size. Not tried on a real phone.

## Collectify 0.32.0: walk round a Card Shop you have to look after, update notices, and pack-opening mistakes you can fix

Android `.apk` only. **The iPhone version is paused until further notice and won't be updated** (the last iPhone build is 0.31.0).

### 🔔 Update notices (opt-in auto update)
- When you open the app it quietly checks whether a newer version is out and shows a banner with the release notes. Tap to see what's new and install it; nothing downloads on its own unless you ask.
- **Opt in to auto update** in About: it downloads new versions in the background (Wi-Fi only by default, and you can allow mobile data), checks the file's checksum, and then just asks you to tap Install. Android always asks before installing, and your data stays.

### ↶ Pack-opening mistakes you can fix
- Sent a card you wanted to the bin? **Take it back with ↶** while you're still going through the pack, change your mind on the summary screen, or, once you have collected, **rescue cards from the dupes bin into any binder** (one copy at a time, added first and removed from the bin only after it is safely in the binder).

### 🚶 Walk round your shop, as your own character
- **A character you design:** skin, hair and colour, top and colour, trousers, hat, glasses, scarf, headphones, a name tag. Dress them in a close-up view, or tap 🧍 any time.
- **Walk with a stick** (or WASD on a computer) or **tap the floor** to walk there round the furniture. Go out of the door onto the pavement and the camera follows you; 🏙️ shows the shop front from the street.
- **Things to do in the shop:** walk over rubbish to sweep it up, stand by the till to serve customers faster, run into a thief to catch them, and tap **Use** on whatever is next to you (a display, the till).

### 🔨 Decorate it, inside and out
- **Inside:** 15 new things (couch, trailer TV, arcade cabinet, capsule machine, vending machine, fish tank with swimming fish, giant plush, standee, statue, wall clock that tells the real time, banners, string lights, a bargain bin, a box pallet and a binder shelf), more floors (dark planks, marble, blue tiles, pink carpet), more walls (mint, plum, wood panels, candy stripes), **lighting moods** (warm, cool, neon, sunset, party) and **one-tap themes**.
- **Outside:** pick the shop front (brick, wood, stucco, stone, teal, pink), awning colour and style, door (glass, wood, double, arched), the sign (board, neon, hanging, marquee) and its colours, string lights, even the street. Put benches, flower boxes, street lamps, an A-frame sign, bunting, a bike rack, a mailbox and a fountain on the pavement. A **sidewalk rack** or **market stall** out front sells to passers-by without them coming inside.
- Decorations add **atmosphere**, and a good-looking shop front adds **curb appeal**; both change what customers think of you.

### 📐 Buy more space
- Make the shop **wider** (two columns at a time) or **deeper** (a row at a time), up to a big flagship store, one strip at a time. The door and counter stay in the middle and your furniture is tidied automatically.

### ✏️ Edit any display, like a binder
- Hang a **name sign** on it, choose its **finish** and **trim colour**, change its **style**, **add shelf tiers** (shelves, racks, trophy cases, pallets), **sort** it (value, price, A to Z, kind, rarity), and **select several items** to move them to another display, reprice them, take them off or feature one on your website. **Move any item to another display** from its price screen.

### 🧰 A shop you have to look after
- **Open and close:** set your opening hours (or open and close by hand). Closed shops get no customers; busy hours are lunch and after school; a **daily event** (Pack Day, Collector's Fair, rain, tournament, street festival) changes who comes.
- **Upkeep:** busy displays **wear out** and stop working until you repair them; customers drop **rubbish** and the shop gets dirty, which earns bad reviews. Sweep, repair, deep clean, or hire a **cleaner**.
- **Bills and staff:** rent and wages come due daily after a few free days; fall too far behind and the shop shuts until you pay. Hire a **cleaner**, a **stocker** (refills empty spots for you) or a **guard**. Autopay is optional.
- **Reputation:** customers leave **reviews** on **your shop's website**, which also shows your rating, what customers think (clean, value, selection, service, atmosphere), your **ranking against rival shops in town** and your visitors. Reply to reviews, feature an item, pick a theme and a tagline.
- **Sell more kinds of things:** sealed **booster boxes**, whole **binders as one lot**, **adult Pokémon**, **eggs**, packs, goods, cards and graded slabs.
- **Contracts:** customers ask for bigger orders (like ten of one pack, a graded card, a Pokémon, a box or a binder lot) and pay well above shelf price if you deliver in time. Accept up to two at once and hand over from your shelves or from what you own.
- **Goals** with coin rewards and a **day report** with an hour-by-hour chart of yesterday's takings. On Android a gentle reminder nudges you when the till is full, bills are due or a contract is running out.

### Tested, and what wasn't
- 173 automated JavaScript tests and 20 Python tests pass (shop rules, simulation, walking and collisions, bills, contracts, reviews, display editing, the all-or-nothing collection changes). The shop was walked round in a browser at phone size, including the shop front, decor, themes, walking out to the street, and opening every new menu.
- **Not tested on a real phone:** the walking controls, the update installer, and how the bigger 3D shop runs on older devices (it lowers its own picture quality if the frame rate drops). The numbers (rent, wages, contract rewards, review frequency) are a first guess: tell me what feels too stingy or too generous.

## Collectify 0.31.0: the Card Shop, binder tags, reliable trades and pulls, and more ways to earn

Android `.apk` and iPhone/iPad `.ipa`, same version, same features.

### 🏪 The Card Shop (new tab)
A 3D shop where everything you collect can earn you coins.
- **Build it your way.** Wall shelves, pack racks, card tables, curio tables, glass cases, Pokémon habitats, binder stands, trophy cases, plants, rugs, posters, a neon sign and lamps. Choose floors and walls, name the shop, and expand from a corner shop up to a flagship store. Tap the floor to place, turn and move.
- **Stock it from the whole game:** booster packs from the Treasure Box, cards you pulled, graded cards (a better grade sells for much more), hatchlings you bred in the nursery, and potions, essences, food, toys and sleeves from the island. Real binder cards can be sold once you tag them 🔁 Tradable, and only leave the binder when they sell. Trophy cases and binder stands show things off, not for sale, and raise your reputation.
- **Customers you can watch:** kids, collectors, trainers, flippers, graders and tourists walk in, browse what suits them, carry it to the counter, queue and pay. Set prices (or tap **Best price**); too high and they walk, a bargain and it flies.
- **Events and orders:** thieves sneak off with things (tap them to catch them for a reward; glass cases are safe, and real cards are never stolen), VIPs want your best card, daily orders pay a bonus, and collectors bring **buy-in offers**: buy a card for less than it's worth, shelve it, sell it for a profit.
- **It earns while you're away.** Up to 8 hours (more with Late opening) of sales while the app is closed; coins wait in the till, and a Cashier empties it for you. Upgrades: marketing, display lighting, fast register, security, cashier, late opening; ad campaigns and a free rush hour bring crowds.

### 🏷️ Binder tags
- Tag cards **Tradable, Gradable, High value, Duplicate, Wishlist** or your own. Badges show on every card in a binder and in the card viewer.
- **Filter inside a binder**, or open the **Tag manager** on the Binders tab: every card from every binder, filtered by tag (any/all) and sorted by **binder, tag, page, rarity or condition** (or value/name). ✨ Smart tagging finds duplicates, high-value and gradable cards. The trade pickers get a **Tradable only** switch, and the binder sorter gains condition and tag.

### 🛡️ Trades and pack pulls you can trust
- **Trades are all-or-nothing:** every card you give is checked against what you offered, then adds and removals happen in one transaction with a retry-safe key, and your binders are read back to confirm. Offered cards are **locked** (🔒) until the trade ends.
- **Opening lots of packs can't lose cards:** every pull is written down first, saved in safe batches, verified, and anything that can't be saved goes to the dupes bin instead. New-versus-duplicate is checked fresh every time, quick-open works on any stack of packs, and the game save now keeps the newest copy if a save to the server was lost.

### 🖼️ Pictures
- Variant printings with no picture of their own (Cracked Ice Holo, Master Ball Pattern and friends, e.g. Dewott 29/114) now show the right art: about **5,600 pictures repaired** in the catalog (v14), and the app repairs any it meets on the fly and once per version walks your binders to fix older entries.
- Cards in your binders survive catalog updates: a card that left the catalog keeps its place, and one that was renumbered is re-pointed at the same card.

### 💰 More ways to earn
- **Four daily tasks** with a bonus for finishing all of them and a streak; **pet upkeep** coins while you're away; **sell duplicates** in one tap (Treasure Box extras and the dupes bin; real, graded and Tradable cards are never sold by accident); and a small **hint when you're idle**: explore the island, care for pets, sell duplicates, restock the shop.

### Tested, and what wasn't
- 123 automated JavaScript tests (shop rules, simulation, glue, tags, income) and 20 Python tests (including the all-or-nothing collection changes and the catalog merge SQL, run against the very statements the apps use) pass; the shop was walked through in a browser at phone size, including building, stocking, selling and a flagship-size shop.
- The Swift (iPhone) side is built and tested by the iOS workflow; the Android Kotlin code is built here. **Not tested on real phones**: the 3D shop may feel heavy on older ones (there is a lite mode), and the numbers (prices, customer counts, upgrade costs) are my best first guess: tell me what feels too slow or too generous.

## Collectify 0.30.0: a bigger island with room to breathe, real paths, and scenery you can change

Android `.apk` and iPhone/iPad `.ipa`, same version, same features.

### 🏝️ A new layout: more room, one or two buildings in view at a time
- The starter island is **much bigger** (about two and a half times the area), and everything now has its own corner:
  - **the farm** to the west, with proper aisles between the rows of plots,
  - **the workshop** to the north,
  - **the market** and the **maid station** to the north-east, a good walk apart,
  - **the yard** to the south-east, with the **food dish, water dish and toy box** well apart,
  - **a pond** to the south-west, and **the windmill** north of the farm in a **clearing of its own** (the trees that crowded it are gone),
  - **the plaza** in the middle, where every road meets.
- Walking is a little faster to match, and a long trip **follows the roads** instead of cutting across the grass.
- The island's zones (Meadow, Orchard, Ranch, Harbor, Summit) sit further out, with their own roads.

### 🛤️ Paths that connect everything, and grow
- Roads run from the **plaza** to the farm (down every aisle), the well, the workshop, the market, the yard and each food dish, water dish and toy box (their little paths **move with them**).
- **New roads appear as you unlock things:** the **maid station's road at level 12**, the **windmill's road** when you buy the windmill, the **Meadow's aisle** with the Meadow, and a road to each new area as the island grows (Orchard, Ranch, Harbor, Summit).
- The roads change as the island grows: **packed dirt, then lighter packed earth, then gravel**, with cobbles set into them. Lamp posts (if you've bought them) line the roads.
- A **signpost in the plaza** points to everywhere you can go, and adds a board for each new place.
- Some small touches: flower planters round the plaza, hay bales, crates and a wheelbarrow at the farm gate.

### 🌊 A pond, and no more walking on water
- A real **pond** with a sandy bank, lily pads, reeds and cattails, ripples that spread, and **fireflies at night**. Water-type Pokémon like to visit it.
- **You (and your Pokémon) can't walk across the pond**, or through trees, rocks, bushes and buildings any more: you slide round them. The Ranch's pond is solid too. If you ever get stuck on something, you sidestep it on your own.

### 🌳 Trees, rocks and bushes are yours to change (Menu → Build → Landscape)
- Every tree, pine, boulder and bush is now part of your island. **Plant** more where you want them (🌳 Oak 🪙40, 🌲 Pine 🪙40, 🪨 Boulder 🪙25, 🌿 Bush 🪙12) with a see-through preview that goes red where it can't go, or switch on **Clear mode** and **tap any tree, rock or bush to remove it** (you get a few coins back, and there's an **Undo**).
- Nothing grows on a **path or a building**, or in the clearings kept free for the places your island will grow into. The island starts out with a belt of forest round the edge and the middle left open.
- Visitors see your scenery as you've arranged it.

### If you already have an island
- **Your crops, buildings, Pokémon, coins and everything in your bag are untouched.** Everything has moved to its new place, with a notice when you open the island.
- The **food dish, water dish and toy box go back to their new default spots** (you can move them again in Decor → Furniture).
- **Decorations that would now sit on a building or a road are put in your Decor stock** (never lost): put them back wherever you like.
- The trees, rocks and bushes are made fresh for the new layout.

### Tested, and what wasn't
- Ten new automated tests (75 in all) check: that every building, plot and path is on the island, that the dishes and toys are apart, that paths appear only when they should and all join up to the plaza and reach every stand point (at every stage of growth), that route planning follows the roads, that the scenery never sits on a road, a building, the windmill's clearing or too close to other things, planting, clearing, refunds and undo, and the move for older islands (decorations put away, dishes reset, notice, only once).
- Tried in a browser at phone size: a brand-new island and a fully grown one from above and on the ground; walking from the start to the workshop, market, maid station, board, farm plots, dishes and the well, round the pond; planting a tree; and clearing a bush by tapping it.
- Not tested on a real phone. The island has many hand-built pieces, so older phones may feel the bigger world. If walking feels too slow or too fast, or something sits in an awkward place, tell me where.

## Collectify 0.29.0: a 3D adventure world, potions and deeper battles

Android `.apk` and iPhone/iPad `.ipa`, same version, same features.

### 🌍 The adventure world is now 3D
- The trails are a little **3D world in the island's own style**: rolling ground with soft colour blending, low-poly trees, and **grass made of real blades** that sway in the wind and **part around your trainer and your partner** as you walk through. Water moves, and **lava glows**.
- **Each region has its own look**, not just its own colours:
  - **Meadow Trail:** round trees, haystacks, flowers, mushrooms, drifting pollen.
  - **Pebble Hills:** snow-capped pines, crystal clusters and boulders, cobbled paths, dust on the wind.
  - **Tide Shore:** palms, a wooden boardwalk, beach umbrellas and giant shells, sea spray.
  - **Dream Grove:** giant glowing mushrooms, runestones and glowing crystals, stepping-stone paths, fireflies.

The effects added in the last few releases were too heavy for many phones. This release removes the biggest costs:

The old "pop" effect (a clipped copy of the artwork shifted over the card) is gone. Cards are now drawn by a WebGL shader:

## Collectify 0.15.0

Installs over your existing Collectify (same signing key) - your binders, wishlist and trades are kept.

### Scanner: fewer nonsense names
- The old scanner read the whole card in one pass and guessed. It now reads several ways, matches the words against the real card names for the game, checks where on the card each word was found, reads collector numbers / set codes, compares the artwork, and combines that into a confidence.
- It says **Confident**, **Likely** or "couldn't read this card" - it no longer fills the list with unrelated cards when the text is unreadable.
- Takes the sharpest of a short burst of frames. OCR engine and English data are bundled, so scanning works offline.
- On our 54-card test set (simulated phone photos) it identified the right card about 65% of the time, against about 24% for the old scanner, with a handful of wrong answers. Real-world results depend on light and focus.
- Scans can take noticeably longer on slow phones than before.

### Camera
- The scanner now starts on the **rear camera**. Change it under the palette button, Preferences.

### Trade
- Rebuilt: one phone shows a QR, the other scans it, and both open the same live trade screen and see each other's cards. Either side can agree or leave; any change resets both agreements. Needs the same Wi-Fi or one phone's hotspot. Offline two-code trading is still there as a fallback.
- Tested here between an Android emulator and a desktop client; not yet tested between two physical phones.
